organizations.publicNote: German record-manufacturing company. Odeon and Parlophon/Parlophone are represented separately as recording labels rather than as variant corporate names.
Recording label within the Lindström group. Export issues used the spelling Parlophone; the label is kept distinct from the corporate body Carl Lindström AG.
Recording label associated with Carl Lindström AG. It is represented separately from the German parent company and from Polskie Zakłady Fonograficzne ‘Odeon’ in Warsaw.

sources.title: Otto Dobrindt — Wikipedia (German)
sources.creator: Wikipedia contributors
sources.researchNote: Records that he joined Carl Lindström AG in 1924 as a recording manager and became its chief recording manager, and that from 1925 he issued his own productions under pseudonyms including Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri, Odeon Tanz-Orchester, Wiener Bohème-Orchester, Dobbri, Robert Renard, Eddie Saxon, Frank Sandlers, Eric Harden and Götz Höhne; his orchestra accompanied Ufa stars on record, among them Hans Albers. These statements follow the secondary Wikipedia article rather than an examination of the original recordings.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11439 a, “Ich weiß ein kleines Café”
sources.fullCitation: Austin Egen, accompanied by the Odeon-Tango-Orchester. “Ich weiß ein kleines Café.” Tango; label credits Dr. B. Kaper and Austin Egen, with words by Fritz Rotter. Odeon O-11439 a, matrix Be 9409; issued May 1931. Label filmed in the YouTube upload by Ilja Livschakoff.
sources.title: Ich weiß ein kleines Café — Odeon O-11439 a
sources.creator: Austin Egen; Odeon-Tango-Orchester
sources.researchNote: Wolfgang Stanicek’s dissertation Austin Egen (2010), p. 156, lists Odeon O-11439a, matrix Be 9409, with Austin Egen and the Odeon-Tango-Orchester: “NE 05/1931” and a Berlin session on 12 March 1931, citing Weihermüller’s Egen discography, p. 380. The structured date describes the May 1931 issue, not the March session. The label in the transfer independently matches the catalogue number, matrix and performers; it also prints “Auch als Tanzplatte geeignet”, B.I.E.M. and Carl Lindström A.-G.

sources.researchNote: The historical span 1928–1933 describes catalogue coverage, not the publication date of the webpage. The list separates general year, recording/session information, release date, matrix and parallel issues where documented, and cites evidence at row level. Those fields are not interchangeable, and an empty release-date cell is not proof of an issue year. A changing total of indexed titles is not included in the bibliographic citation. The heading’s copyright stamp is not treated as an independently verified publication or update date.
